title: PRAGMATA Sketchbook (Demo)
provenance: user report on Highball (highball-db#1, OdynOOb) — Apple M4, macOS 15.7.3, wine-10.0 Sikarugir r6 flacknabe-cpu (highball-db#485, 2026-10-14), Apple M1 Pro 16 GB, macOS 26.7, Highball 0.10.15, engine x64-sikarugir10.0_6-r26, D3DMetal 3 with a modified D3DMetal, DXVK environment, Metal HUD, 60 fps cap, recipes steam and vcrun2022, rated 3 of 5 after 12 minutes, gameplay and combat at 20 to 60 fps. flacknabe-cpu again (highball-db#485, 2026-10-16): Highball 0.10.16, engine x64-crossover26.3-r25, the original D3DMetal 3, HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, the demo launches and reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro. Not verified by the maintainer.
notes: Capcom's RE Engine, DirectX 12 only, so it needs D3DMetal (DXMT translates Direct3D 11 and is rightly refused). On an M1 Pro the game stops at its graphics check because D3DMetal answers no to 64-bit atomics on descriptor heap resources (D3D12 OPTIONS11), the same check as the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo and Kunitsu-Gami. A player patched that answer inside D3DMetal and reached gameplay and combat at 20 to 60 fps, which says the game does not need the feature to draw. Highball cannot ship a modified D3DMetal. On an M4 D3DMetal 3 already answers yes (measured here 2026-10-14 with a probe), so newer chips may pass the check as they are. On Highball's Wine 11 engine r25 (0.10.16) the variable HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1 makes Highball's DirectX 12 layer answer yes, and the demo reaches gameplay on the M1 Pro with the original D3DMetal (confirmed by the reporter, highball-db#485). The recipe sets both. An earlier report (M4, macOS 15.7, engine r6) crashed at thread start on D3DMetal; it predates every current engine.

knownIssues.symptom: Unsupported graphics card error at start, then the game quits (M1 Pro)
knownIssues.cause: D3DMetal reports AtomicInt64OnDescriptorHeapResourceSupported as false on M1 chips, and RE Engine requires it
knownIssues.fix: the recipe: Wine 11 engine r25 or later with HB_TSSHIM_ATOMIC64=1, which has Highball's layer in front of D3DMetal answer yes (confirmed on an M1 Pro, highball-db#485)
